title: Maracanã: Flamengo Accuses Vasco and Palmeiras of Pitch Damage
seoTitle: Flamengo accuses Vasco and Palmeiras of damaging Maracanã.
subtitle: The legal battle over the stadium gains new chapters with Flamengo's claim.
excerpt: The Maracanã is at the center of a new legal controversy as Flamengo formally accuses Vasco and Palmeiras of damaging the stadium's turf during an April match.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The Maracanã returned to the spotlight in Brazilian sport due to a new chapter in the legal dispute over its use. Flamengo filed a petition with the 47th Civil Court of the Rio de Janeiro State Court, formally accusing Vasco and Palmeiras of causing "serious damage" and leaving the stadium's turf "full of holes" after an April 2023 clash.

The legal fight over stadium usage

This Flamengo filing is part of a broader legal battle that began with Vasco. The Cruzmaltino club seeks to secure a definitive right to use the public stadium under the same commercial conditions as Flamengo and Fluminense. On August 18, Judge Lorena Dutra had already ruled in Vasco's favor, confirming that the injunction obtained by the club was correct, that public safety justified the stadium choice, and that the event did not harm public assets.

Flamengo's accusation regarding the pitch

Unhappy with the court decision that recognized Vasco's right, Flamengo attached a technical report from Greenleaf in an attempt to overturn the ruling. The red‑black club claimed that the specific match caused injury risk for the athletes involved and ripped the field. To support its argument, Flamengo cited contemporary news items and statements from Vasco's technical staff that highlighted the poor condition of the Maracanã turf, seeking to justify its stance on the stadium’s management.

The April 2023 confrontation in question

The match at the heart of the accusation took place on April 23, 2023, on the Maracanã pitch. Vasco and Palmeiras met in a second‑round Brazilian Championship duel that ended 2‑2. Vasco’s goals were scored by Pedro Raul and Gabriel Pec, while Rafael Navarro and Artur replied for the São Paulo side. The game attracted nearly 60,000 spectators. At the end of that season, Palmeiras celebrated the national title with 70 points, and Vasco secured its stay in Série A. Flamengo, meanwhile, finished the year without major trophies.

Developments in the judicial arena

Flamengo’s petition, alleging pitch damage, represents a new development in the complex legal dispute over the Maracanã. The Gávea club’s strategy is to contest the earlier decision that favored Vasco, aiming to overturn the Cruzmaltino’s right to use the stadium on equal terms. The case remains under review in the 47th Civil Court of the Rio de Janeiro State Court, keeping the future of Maracanã’s use on the agenda of debates and judicial decisions.

Information from Papo na Colina, ge.
